# 2027 Carnival Champions' Parade at the Sambadrome

In the evening, after a day of sightseeing in Rio de Janeiro, you will leave your hotel for the Sambadrome. This is where the Carnival Champions' Parade takes place, featuring samba schools in dazzling costumes, musical ensembles and moving floats.

The performance continues throughout the night. From the stands, you will have an excellent view of the procession, dance routines and elaborate decorations. After the parade ends, a transfer will take you back to your hotel.

The price of this excursion as part of the tour includes admission to the Champions' Parade and round-trip hotel — Sambadrome — hotel transfers.

Lapa draws crowds with its famous arches and welcoming bars, where live samba, bossa nova and other Latin American melodies fill the open air. Here, music and dance become a way of communicating, and the streets are full of energy and sparkling joy. Time seems to stand still, and nights feel endless. Lapa is a whirlwind of emotions, with something for everyone, from street parties and performances by buskers to sophisticated cocktails in atmospheric bars.

## The Rhythms of Rio After Dark

Lapa is Rio's exuberant nightlife district, packed with bars and clubs to suit every taste. Crowds of young people and visitors of all ages are out having fun. Music of every kind, from techno to live traditional sounds, pours out from all directions.

Brazil's national music is endlessly varied, from African traditions brought here by enslaved Black people to bossa nova, created in the middle of the last century by white composers. Amid cobblestone streets, old monasteries and the historic Arcos da Lapa aqueduct, an informal and free-spirited social scene thrives. If you want a lively night out and are not afraid of adventure, this is the place to be!

Lapa's nightlife venues are hardly just bars. They form a succession of dance halls: as you leave one to enter another, you find yourself in the thick of a festive crowd. The signature local drink is the caipirinha, a mixture of cachaça, a sugarcane spirit, lime juice, ice and sugar.

## Tour Details

Duration: 4 hours. Drinks are included. Transfers and the services of a Russian-speaking guide are available at an additional cost.

The price is per person. Discounts may be available for groups of more than one person; contact us to discuss.

In the evening, you can attend a show featuring live music and dance. A guide will pick you up at your hotel and accompany you to the venue, where dancers in bright costumes perform to live music and drums.

The show combines samba and capoeira, including acrobatics and martial-arts movements. If you wish, you can order dinner featuring traditional Brazilian dishes. After the performance, you will return to your hotel.

The shared group tour with an English-speaking guide costs $90 per person. The private option with a Russian-speaking guide costs $170 per person, with a minimum of 2 participants.
